notes.content: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4778592/0d3b705bacc35862b7e32f2acc5ac563d6ca2602.png"][/img][/p][p]First announced during our 10th Anniversary celebrations, the now-named Retouched Update for Dying Light is now live! So, if you want to rediscover the origins of the virus, replay through Kyle Crane’s origin story or enjoy Harran again, there’s never been a better time.[/p][p][/p][p]What exactly has arrived with the Retouched Update?[/p][list][*][p]Higher resolution textures[/p][/*][*][p]Upscaled skyboxes & clouds[/p][/*][*][p]“Ultra”-level quality shadows[/p][/*][*][p]Fully remastered soundtrack from the original composer, Paweł Błaszczak[/p][/*][*][p]New tracks and ambient themes added to the game[/p][/*][/list][p]Please note: The exact changes may vary by platform.[/p][p][/p][p]If you want to get into the more technical side, make sure to check out the latest [url="https://pilgrimoutpost.techlandgg.com/news/ten-years-later-still-going-strong-dying-light-retouched-update-releasing-june-26"]DevBlog [/url]which will certainly cover what you want to know.[/p][p]And this is just part of our commitment to making the Dying Light experience even better, so watch this space![/p][p]So, go see the enhancements for yourself and jump back into the shoes of Kyle in preparation for Dying Light: The Beast being unleashed on August 22![/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/239140/Dying_Light/"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3008130/Dying_Light_The_Beast/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Ten Years Later - Dying Light: Retouched Update Releasing June 26
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4778592/4b65adf7113a1975d9ad6684ec7e679f9a2205da.jpg"][/img][/p][p]It's been an absolutely wild month here at Techland! We're in the thick of what I'm calling the "Summer of Dying Light," delivering updates and big news across all three Dying Light games. Just a few weeks ago, we dropped the first gameplay for Dying Light: The Beast, revealed its release date, and kicked off pre-orders (if you haven't seen it, check out my [u][url="https://pilgrimoutpost.techlandgg.com/news/to-our-incredible-dying-light-community"]last dev blog[/url][/u]). I'm incredibly proud of what we're building with The Beast - it’s the culmination of more than 10 years of experience in open-world survival horror![/p][p][/p][p]But here's the thing: we never forget where we came from. That's why, this week, we're not just looking forward - we're rolling out significant updates for both the original Dying Light and Dying Light 2: Stay Human. We promised to support our games for a long time, and we're committed to continuing that support, right through and beyond the launch of Dying Light: The Beast.[/p][h1]Let’s be clear: Enhancements, not Remaster![/h1][p]Back in January, when we celebrated the 10th Anniversary of Dying Light, I announced that we are working on a new update for the original Dying Light. Ten years later and the game that started it all is still going strong! When I looked online the day after the video, my heart skipped a beat. Quite a few of you were expecting a full remaster of some sort.[/p][p][/p][p]So, let's set the record straight: the Retouched Update is about squeezing out even more from the Dying Light you already love. It’s not a complete overhaul or remaster.[/p][p][/p][p]Even without the update, Dying Light still holds up pretty well - just imagine that it’s 10 years old! But to truly explain what we've changed, I sat down with the brilliant minds who made it happen: Grzegorz Świstowski, our Technical Game Director, and Krzysztof Knefel, Lead 3D Artist: [/p][p][/p][p]"One of the best things about working with your own engine is that the people building it are just next door," explains Grzegorz Świstowski, our Technical Game Director. "Over the past couple of years, we've added a lot, customized a lot, and learned how to squeeze more from the tech we already have. One day, someone just started applying those learnings to some old assets - and it just clicked that we could do that across the whole game."[/p][p][/p][p]So we put some more people on it. We started increasing texture quality of surroundings and upscaling them to create a sharper, better look in the game. “It was a lot of manual work - but increasing the texture resolution or quality can have a huge impact on how the environment appears on screen,” said Krzysztof Knefel. Just look at the comparison of these wooden wall panels![/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-qw.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdh6eblfNxrJFLIfbK1N3nS5QjaoBvldcH5OOWa3WzeCOoOgH_QTxyBDDwI9ilKb9PWQGvJIPTCgdCpCwDk8Ff31CsQtpkSuVYMvY7PJ931CcVa6qUQqmE35eS-dJyPHRagqoNJNw?key=7iRazORO0HHrNdorPYrULw"][/img][/p][p]Krzysztof spent a lot of time by manually adjusting and tweaking assets, squeezing out every last bit of visual quality. A big part of this involved improving lighting and PBR (physics based rendering). “With so many years of experience with PBR we're improving how metallic surfaces reflect light or react physically to the world which makes them look a lot more realistic!” You can see the difference on the metal hangar walls below. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-qw.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdxOcIzHoZGhV9V0kj-D39E-gex28RzYoZELjbbYhS6bBRtb7SaGGVES23lTICK6eeJfdJmdTGkj_jRuulRRcmvWZJsjivpH0cDulI7pXvUOxcmYz3042pDwsP4NaLg9WF1XjsHqw?key=7iRazORO0HHrNdorPYrULw"][/img][/p][p]We also made some smaller tweaks and changes to the code that have a big impact on details in Harran. “We’ve increased the maximum LOD (level of detail) range from 260% to 340% in the view distance menu in the game options. This means players who are running on modern and better systems can increase the distance of highly detailed assets being loaded into the game and balance increased GPU/CPU load on their own,” explains Grzegorz Świstowski. [/p][p][/p][p]But one of the biggest differences will be visible on floors and cement walls. We’re introducing a new 8K Ultra shadow quality and improved the lighting options of many surfaces and with these new shadows, a lot of surfaces that previously looked rather flat now really pop out and get depth! [/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-qw.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXczrAa48HkI2VYHnrfe6PwmCrHZRMXO31oZsxfQ4vdlhF6nGCTShSG42wEAmM4O5vbK0-Fxe-E6CKa20SDECPw8oheccOxO0KKC1hn0J7lPpaKyB2849kPRwkqUA3Mrz9B6amgvPg?key=7iRazORO0HHrNdorPYrULw"][/img][/p][h1]The Sound of Harran[/h1][p]Beyond just how it looks, we wanted to dial up the very atmosphere of Harran. Sound and music is crucial for immersion, and we’ve gone all out to make it an experience. The maestro himself, Paweł Blaszczak, the original composer, came back to give the soundtrack a complete remaster. Get this: he even recreated that retro-tape sound by actually recording on tape! Talk about dedication. It’s authentic, nostalgic, and absolutely fantastic. [/p][p][/p][p]We’ve woven in brand new tracks and ambient sounds throughout the game, deepening the mood and cranking up the tension as you explore. And we seriously juiced up the hit reaction audio in combat. Every swing, every crunch, every zombie takedown will sound more satisfying, more impactful. You’ll feel those hits.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="abQYwONaKgk;full"][/previewyoutube][h1]Why it took a while[/h1][p]A lot of you have been asking in the last few months about the Retouched Update - where it was, why it was taking so long. The honest answer is this: We were working with 10+ year old technology. Even with all the new experience we've gained over the years, figuring out how to apply those learnings to the original Dying Light engine while keeping everything stable was a challenge.[/p][p][/p][p]And let me tell you, it was a massive amount of manual work. Krzysztof literally became the undisputed master of Harran: "I basically walked through the entire map, looking for assets to be improved. And all of those had to be changed manually by our artists."[/p][p][/p][p]Crucially, we also made it a top priority not to change the game's system requirements. "You can't just crank up the details and hope it still works on everyone's system," Grzegorz explains. "Especially on consoles – we were testing endlessly to ensure we didn't run out of memory on last-gen consoles." It was a delicate balancing act, but we cracked it. And now? It's finally ready![/p][h1]Explore Kyle Crane’s origin story with this free update[/h1][p]The Dying Light: Retouched Update will be completely free for all Dying Light owners on PC, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S and will roll out on June 26, 2025. The level of changes may vary by platform. [/p][p][/p][p]With the update out before the release of Dying Light: The Beast it’s the best time to jump right back into Kyle Crane’s origin story if you haven’t played Dying Light yet. And even if you have, it’s worth heading back to Harran. [/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="M0GCr2P9510;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Good night. And good luck![/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/239140/Dying_Light/"][/dynamiclink]

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3008130/Dying_Light_The_Beast/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Dying Light: The Beast Releases August 22, 2025
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4778592/ae695a2782a22dfe72b3dbee5d834b4623f7d21d.png[/img]
Want to see what awaits you in this open world action survival horror? Check out the first gameplay trailer we just dropped and get a taste for the most beautiful zombie apocalypse, the scenic setting of Castor Woods and more. Releasing on August 22, 2025 on PC, PlayStation 5 Pro, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, Dying Light: The Beast will test your survival instincts and nerve like nothing else!

[previewyoutube=M0GCr2P9510;full][/previewyoutube]

To increase your odds of outlasting the night and seeing the next sunrise, pre-order the game now to get the Hero of Harran Bundle as a bonus. And, of course, Dying Light 2: Stay Human Ultimate Edition owners will automatically get this bundle for The Beast, too!

[b]Hero of Harran Bundle[/b]
Taking a trip through Castor Woods is a deadly detour for most people. Well, you’re not “most people”, especially with the Hero of Harran Bundle in your arsenal. Transform these terrains into your personal playground with its weapons, all while looking like a true post-apo survivor! Are you ready to take on Castor Woods?

The Hero of Harran Bundle features a set of items that won’t just help you in Castor Woods, but also honors the legacy of the Dying Light franchise. Some of them might just bring back the memories of your time in Harran:

[list]
[*] [b]Ultimate Survivor Outfit[/b] – Known as the Juggernaut outfit in Dying Light, this cool makeshift apocalyptic look was rewarded to the most dedicated survivors.
[*] [b]Harran Combat Knife (+ upgradable Blueprint)[/b] – A swift and deadly weapon, the zombie head engraving on the blade is a throwback to the original Dying Light’s box art.
[*] [b]The Follower Crossbow (+ upgradable Blueprint)[/b] – First found in Dying Light: The Following expansion, this crossbow is perfect for a stealthier approach. 
[*] [b]In Jade’s Memory Pistol (+ upgradable Blueprint)[/b] – Jade Aldemir - she’s one of the reasons you made it out of Harran alive. With her likeness on the grip, think of her with every bullet you fire from this pistol.
[*] [b]Castor Woods Patrol [/b] – Rescuing hikers from the woods and cats from trees was a breeze for this powerful beast. Now put it to the real test and see how it handles the zombie apocalypse!
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4778592/fc3ad26a0a06c82bf5ce72f3c914763e816313d4.jpg[/img]

[b]CONFRONT YOUR INNER BEAST TO UNLEASH THE HERO WITHIN[/b]

You are Kyle Crane, equal parts monster and survivor… for now. Praised as the “Hero of Harran” and a man who sacrificed himself to the point of infection, you became target no. 1 for the Baron’s brutal, beastly experiments. After being used as a human guinea pig for more than a decade and having your DNA spliced with zombie strains, you break out.

But you are not free. Now, an internal conflict begins as the virus takes over: it’s man vs. monster. You want more than anything to return to the old you, but he’s all but gone. However, you can still find the strength to make sure your human DNA remains dominant. And while these primal beast-like abilities may be seen as a curse, they may just give you the upper hand in your quest for revenge and, ultimately, rip the man who did this to you apart. One. Limb. At. A. Time.

And to do that, you’re going to need some help and this just might be the way to bring the old Crane back: the citizens of Castor Woods are in dire need of a savior and you’re their only hope. They’re counting on you as this world has turned against them. Can a beast be a hero in this world? Only if you can take control of it.

[b]A ZOMBIE APOCALYPSE HAS NEVER LOOKED THIS BEAUTIFUL[/b]

Castor Woods, a place of beauty and a once idyllic location to visit. That was until the outbreak. Now, few people call this place home, but plenty of zombies and hidden dangers do. This region has its stories, but no one left to tell them, so investigate what lies beneath its facades, discover mementos of days gone and uncover secrets that were never meant to be revealed. Just remember: you might not like what you find. Is there anything more eerily beautiful?

But Castor Woods is more than just natural beauty. Take in the location, its fresh air and charm and you’ll understand that this varied landscape allows you to find your own way around the valley. Sneak through the gloomy forests and woodland, venture into the open swamps and wetlands, or if you’re lucky enough to find a working truck, jump in and put the pedal to the metal.

Lose yourself in this living and breathing locale, that’s so real you can feel the tension in the air. Experience dynamic and unpredictable weather that will affect how you play as it impacts your visibility, your environments and even how enemies behave. Plus, use the realistic interactions with your surroundings to your advantage: set a fire to burn your enemies, just maybe don’t try it in the middle of a rainstorm, or combine electricity with water to give your foes a shock.

[b]THE MOST OPEN SURVIVAL HORROR YET[/b]

Dying Light: The Beast is unlike anything else in the genre. Building tension beyond narrow corridors or tight spaces, discover an experience that blends open-world freedom with intense, atmospheric survival horror, brutal combat and natural movement.

In this world, fear has nowhere to hide. To keep yourself alive to see another day, you’ll need to use all the tools in your arsenal. Outmaneuver enemies with your parkour skills, tear them limb from limb with visceral melee moves or bring out the big guns, like a UV grenade launcher or flamethrower. But never forget: ammo is a rarity here. 

Surviving the day is a challenge, but the night is a whole nother beast. This is when the series’ apex predators, the Volatiles, come out to play. You’re in their domain now and your chances of survival have dramatically dropped, so don’t forget, running is a valid tactic; your movement skills will allow you to navigate Castor Woods like no one else can. Climb, leap and run across the open world and you might just make it to the temporary sanctuary of a safe zone instead of an early grave. But if you have to fight, you can always unleash the beast to head straight to the top of the food chain!

notes.title: Dying Light 2 Stay Human Returns to Its Roots with Good Night, Good Luck Update
notes.content:
[b]DYING LIGHT 2 STAY HUMAN IS ON SALE![/b]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/534380/Dying_Light_2_Stay_Human/][b]Save up to 50% on Dying Light 2 Stay Human during the Steam Summer Sale![/b][/url]
Play it now and enjoy tons of post-launch content.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4778592/6ea5150d4e0108b6f1d758d14e3f9c7a500db471.png[/img]

[b]In the Dead of Night[/b]

The day and night cycle has always been at the heart of our franchise, and we want players to fear going out once the sun’s set. The nights in Villedor are not just darker but also scarier, thanks to the Volatiles that now roam the streets. [b]These apex predators were part of what made the nighttime so dangerous in Dying Light, and we know players wanted this sense of dread to return with Dying Light 2 Stay Human.[/b] Before this update, the nights were never safe, but they felt manageable… Now, you'll be lucky to make it to sunrise.

[b]Give It a Good Run[/b]

Sometimes the only way to survive is to run away. We've further improved the parkour by adding new animations, increased control in the air, and more momentum between movements. 

While [b]parkour is the highlight of Dying Light 2 Stay Human[/b], some experienced players wanted it to be [b]more challenging[/b]. We responded to this feedback by introducing a new parkour style, Physical Parkour, specifically designed to cater to these wishes. Now, you can select in the Settings menu whether you’d like to have more control over your movement, for a grounded and intense journey, or go with the assisted gameplay.

[b]New Color Grading Options and More[/b]

We’ve also added two [b]new color grading options: “Harran Sunset” and “Darker Nights”[/b], and extra graphics options for those playing on Ultra settings. Additionally, you’ll now be able to throw weapons and retrieve them later. And finally, we have introduced some UI modifications and added more transmog options.

[b]The Summer of Horrors[/b]

[b]In Dying Light 2 Stay Human, the next few months will be full of events, crossovers, and updates, as we celebrate the Summer of Horrors.[/b] Our next event will be Bloody Nights, where you’ll be tasked with looting valuables dotted around Villedor, all while trying to hide from and escape those pesky Volatiles! Throughout the event, they will grow in both power and number, so you will need to keep your wits about you! For your efforts, you’ll be duly rewarded with some must-have items, including Hakon’s Crossbow and The Prick’s Outfit. [b]Bloody Nights will be available until 16:00 CEST on July 13.[/b]

What’s coming next with the Summer of Horrors? Well, we’re partnering with a fellow iconic zombie franchise: The Walking Dead! Get ready to have Lucille and Michonne’s Katana in your hands, and much, much more!

notes.title: A free weekend and a special event for Dying Light's anniversary!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4778592/d6bc35feafe3b0764b651dd95e348803b722cf69.png[/img]
Time flies when you’re having fun, and so the last [b]six years[/b] of Dying Light passed by at the double. Thank you for being with us! We’re not slowing down, though, as we plan to deliver even more hours of joy, starting right away. Pop the champagne and celebrate six years of Dying Light with a [b]free weekend on Steam[/b] and [b]the Zombie Hunt event[/b]!

If you or any of your friends still haven’t tried Dying Light, there couldn’t be a better time to fix that! [b]From February 25, you’ll be able to play Dying Light for free on Steam for the entire weekend[/b]. Explore Harran, the post-apocalyptic city taken over by zombies. Master parkour and combat skills, learn crafting and fight the infected, as you unravel the mysteries of a deadly infection. Want to play with friends? Try the co-op mode! Test it out, and if you enjoy the game and choose to continue your adventure, you’ll keep all the progress you’ve made!

[previewyoutube=s1Tk-GVGpWY;full][/previewyoutube]

Although we’re celebrating, the citizens of Harran are still in grave danger. A while ago, the GRE sent their agents into the field, equipping them with special boost potions—the “GREcipe”. Unfortunately, the mission didn’t go off as planned and the operatives died. Now, they walk around Harran as undead, terrorizing the city and wreaking havoc among survivors. And that’s not all. Since the “GREcipe” caused mutations in their bodies, [b]they are not just some regular undead, but tough and strong freaks of nature[/b]. It’s going to take skill and wit to hunt them down, but the bounty is generous. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4778592/64d57b681ca14b81e2e7aa1bb311d0dbe7ec21b5.jpg[/img]
First, find and pacify [b]Hothead Joe[/b], an undead HTU officer. You’ll recognize him by his size and the HTU helmet. [b]Defeat him, and you’ll be free to loot his “HyperArgument” hammer[/b] as well as other higher-level items. [b]Being a special goon[/b], he'll also grant you [i]a significant XP boost each time you kill him[/i]! When on your way, make sure to also [b]help the survivors scattered around Harran[/b]. Assist them, and if the community reaches the goal, you'll be rewarded with [b]a gold weapon[/b]! You’ve got one week to deal with Joe and save the survivors, as another freak of nature is already approaching, and he'll be here soon.

notes.title: Celebrate the Chinese New Year with Dying Light’s Lunar Event!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4778592/e864146e983be337fad0354a288e3818146e9ba7.jpg[/img]
A Chinese legend says there was once a ferocious creature called Nián. It would emerge from the sea by the end of every lunar year to wreak havoc and feast on animals and humans. It kept coming back, until the villagers learned it was terrified of loud noises, fire, and the color red. That is how the bright and loud Chinese New Year festivities were born—from the villagers’ efforts to ward off the beast.

[previewyoutube=gWmqLVpm654;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Let’s welcome the Year of the Ox with a bang[/b] to make sure Nián keeps away from Harran. Dress for the occasion with the free Ox Warrior bundle, stuff your pockets full of trap bombs (we’ve increased their damage for the duration of the Lunar Event) and go make some noise in the streets by [b]blowing zombies to pieces[/b]. Don’t worry if you can’t craft your own trap bombs – the Quartermasters will supply you daily with 3 pieces of each variant (exploding, shrapnel, toxic). While you’re at it, be sure to pick up some [b]fireworks as well. Available only during the event[/b], these special items will lure monsters like regular firecrackers, then set them aflame as they go off and illuminate the sky with dazzling pyrotechnics. Talk about mixing pleasure with business!

Kill enough zombies with trap bombs and fireworks to [b]complete your personal bounty and claim the gold Leaping Tiger Dao as a reward[/b] – forged especially for the occasion. Land at least 3 consecutive hits with this beautiful sword, and its blade will light up with ancient power that grants you a damage boost. Don’t stop there, though, because partying hard will really pay off. [b]If the community reaches its goal, everyone who contributed will earn 3 King Mods[/b]. How’s that for kicking off the new lunar year?

notes.title: Save Christmas in Dying Light's Winter Event
notes.content:
[h2]Super-Crane saves Christmas in Dying Light’s Winter Event[/h2]

The undead are trying to ruin Christmas, but fear not, because Super-Crane is back to save the day! Make children in Harran happy by collecting as many presents as you can and delivering them to quartermasters. You’ll find lost gifts in airdrops, Rais’ supply stashes, and quarantine zones, but some got stolen by mischievous Bolters. These scoundrels will make a run for it as soon as they see you (and damn, they’re fast!) but that’s when Super-Crane’s enhanced grappling hook comes in handy.
[previewyoutube=xn3iuwANq9k;full][/previewyoutube]
Tiny Goblin Zombies on the other hand chase you on sight. They might look cute in their little green jackets and striped pants, but you’ll quickly learn they are mean! Just like thieving Bolters, they’re more numerous in Old Town than the Slums, but instead of presents they drop Christmas Snacks that grant you various short-lasting buffs. You can consume those treats right away or you can use them to make Grandma’s Eggnog that temporarily boosts your stamina, armor, and speed. To be able to do that, you’ll need to complete your personal bounty, as it rewards you with blueprints for Grandma’s Eggnog, Snowball (a throwable that freezes enemies in place), and the Santa’s Helper outfit. If the community collects enough presents before the event ends at 19:00 CET on January 2, you will also receive a docket for the Candy Cane weapon blueprint.

Have fun playing around with your grappling hook as you strive to restore the Christmas spirit in Harran!
